name: Huaxcaleca Nahuatl
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: No grammar/phonology of Huaxcaleca Nahuatl found; SIL Mexico page yielded nothing on acento

sources.citation: Lingmex: Bibliografía Lingüística de México desde 1970 (El Colegio de México), simple search via JSON endpoint for 'Chichiquila', 'Chilchotla', 'Huaxcaleca', 'Quimixtlán' (control 'Zongolica' = 13 hits).
sources.note: 0 records for this variety; no thesis, article or vocabulary on Chichiquila/Chilchotla Nahuatl is registered.

sources.citation: Tuggy, David. n.d. 'Silabación y acento en el náhuatl'. SIL México web page (family-level Nahuatl overview).
sources.note: FAMILY-LEVEL only, not about nhq: 'El acento normal del náhuatl cae en la penúltima sílaba, o sea, las palabras del náhuatl generalmente son graves. Sin embargo, en algunas variantes del náhuatl hay situaciones en las que el acento recae en la última o antepenúltima sílaba.' SIL Mexico's Nahuatl family page lists no nhq variant and no nhq publications.

sources.citation: Repository sweeps (all read online, 2026-09-17): Universidad Veracruzana cdigital.uv.mx API; BUAP repositorio API (only Mejía Gutiérrez 2023 'Los topónimos municipales en náhuatl del estado de Puebla'); Repositorio UNAM; INAH/ENAH repositorio; CIESAS repositorio; COLMEX repositorio; Dialnet; Estudios de Cultura Náhuatl OJS; Tlalocan OJS; Crossref; archive.org; es/en Wikipedia.
sources.note: no linguistic description of Chichiquila/Huaxcaleca Nahuatl found in any of them; es.wikipedia 'Náhuatl' has a 3-sentence 'Náhuatl de Chichiquila' paragraph derived from Ethnologue, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: INALI. 2008. Catálogo de las lenguas indígenas nacionales, agrupación náhuatl, variante 'mexicano (del oriente de Puebla)'.
sources.note: nothing; identity only (municipios Chichiquila incl. Huaxcaleca, and Chilchotla).
nothing; gives location (Puebla: Chichiquila, Chilchotla), 7,000 speakers (1990), 87% intelligibility of Sierra de Puebla Nahuatl, 85% of Orizaba Nahuatl.

sources.citation: Lastra de Suárez, Yolanda. 1986. Las áreas dialectales del náhuatl moderno (Serie Antropológica 62). México: UNAM-IIA. 766 pp. — questionnaire locality Chichiquila, Puebla (stress-marked phonetic transcriptions) and Part I discussion of rasgos fonológicos by subarea.

sources.note: The only published primary linguistic data on Chichiquila Nahuatl known to Glottolog/ASJP; its transcriptions and trait tables would show whether stress is regular penultimate at this point. One copy would also serve many other uncatalogued Nahuatl varieties.
